import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv', names=['sepal_length', 'sepal_width', 'petal_length', 'petal_width', 'species'])

# Map species to numerical values for visualization
species_map = {'setosa': 0, 'versicolor': 1, 'virginica': 2}
data['species'] = data['species'].map(species_map)

# Create a pairplot to visualize the relationship between features
sns.pairplot(data, hue='species', palette='husl')
plt.title('Relationship Between Iris Flower Features')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Reset the figure for the next plot
plt.clf()

# Create a boxplot to compare the distribution of features across species
sns.boxplot(data=data, x='species', y='sepal_length', palette='husl')
plt.title('Distribution of Sepal Length Across Iris Species')
plt.xlabel('Iris Species')
plt.ylabel('Sepal Length (cm)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
